labs.title: Building a Status Importer That Rejects Stale Data and Unproven Completion Claims
labs.summary: A local importer that accepts only the metadata a status brief needs, rejects stale or content-bearing records, and will not claim work is done without an artifact.

labs.title: Requiring Confirmation Before a Voice Command Starts an Agent Job
labs.summary: A local confirmation gate that treats a voice transcription as untrusted and starts an agent job only after the owner confirms the exact proposal.

labs.title: Building a Status Record That Holds No Message Content and Expires
labs.summary: A strict status record for tasks that stores metadata only, rejects stale or malformed entries, and never counts as proof of completion.

labs.title: Checking a Config Change Actually Reached the Running Service
labs.summary: Compares the wanted setting with the running process's environment, its log and its status endpoint, showing that a changed file alone proves nothing.

labs.title: Letting Automation Add a Calendar Event Only When the Message Proves It
labs.summary: A fixture-driven pipeline that writes a calendar event only when the source message supports the date, time and action.

labs.title: Reviewing an Agent Tool Bundle for Least Privilege
labs.summary: Reviews the tools an inbound messaging agent can actually use and removes the ones that are unnecessary or hold credentials.

labs.title: Testing an AI Agent's Final Message, Not Its First Draft
labs.summary: Builds a local test harness that judges what an AI agent would finally send after tool calls, filtering and rewriting, instead of the model's first output.

labs.title: Assessing a Found USB Drive Without Plugging It In
labs.summary: Google Cybersecurity Certificate exercise: assessing a found USB drive as a data-leak and malware risk without connecting it.

labs.title: Reviewing a Payroll Change Through Access-Control Evidence
labs.summary: Google Cybersecurity Certificate worksheet: analysing a simulated payroll change, what the logs prove about who made it, and which access controls failed.

labs.title: Proving Two Identical-Looking Files Are Not the Same File
labs.summary: Google Cybersecurity Certificate activity: using sha256sum and cmp to show that two files which look identical are different.

labs.title: Decrypting a Caesar Cipher and an AES-256 File in Linux
labs.summary: Google Cybersecurity Certificate activity: finding and decrypting a Caesar-cipher file, then using OpenSSL to decrypt an AES-256 file.

labs.title: Completing a SQL Join for a Security Incident Investigation
labs.summary: Google Cybersecurity Certificate activity: INNER, LEFT and RIGHT joins across machines, employees and login attempts to investigate an incident.

labs.title: SQL Time-Window Filtering for Authentication Triage
labs.summary: Turning an authentication or patching question into SQL filters on dates, times and IDs, based on Google Cybersecurity Certificate material.

labs.title: Verifying a Local-Only HTTP Service Cannot Be Reached or Misused
labs.summary: Builds a toy HTTP service meant to be reachable only from the same machine and to run one fixed action, then attacks those assumptions.

labs.title: Verifying an Encrypted Backup Restore Safely
labs.summary: Checks that an encrypted backup really restores: restore to an isolated location, inspect it, and avoid starting a second live copy.

labs.title: Testing an Agent Relay That Refuses Stale or Replayed Messages
labs.summary: Tests the integrity checks in a local relay between agents, using fixtures only, so old or repeated messages are refused.

labs.title: Allowing Exactly One Reply per Incoming Message
labs.summary: A small authorization pattern for automation that messages people: each incoming message permits one short-lived reply to one destination.

labs.title: Building a Minimal Adversarial Test Harness for a Chat Persona
labs.summary: A script that sends the same adversarial prompt to a chatbot many times, measures how often the answer changes, and scores what it reveals about itself.

labs.title: SELECT, FROM, and ORDER BY for Login-Activity Review
labs.summary: Google Cybersecurity Certificate activity: basic SELECT and FROM queries, with ORDER BY to put login events in time order.

labs.title: Filtering SQL Queries with WHERE and LIKE
labs.summary: Google Cybersecurity Certificate activity: narrowing SQL results with WHERE and LIKE to the records a security task needs.

labs.title: Building and Breaking an SSRF-Safe Fetch Guard
labs.summary: Builds a small guard that stops a program fetching internal addresses, then attacks it the way two real bypasses were found.

labs.title: Assessing a Candidate Tool Before Adoption
labs.summary: A security-first review of a third-party command-line tool before installing it: its source, permissions, what it keeps, and how to remove it.

labs.title: Isolating Parallel Agents with Git Worktrees
labs.summary: Uses git worktrees so several automated agents can work on one repository at once without touching each other's files.

labs.title: Testing Safe File Delivery: Expiring Links and Hash Checks
labs.summary: Tests the checks behind handing over a task's output file safely: single-purpose expiring links, hash verification and revocation.

labs.title: Auditing What an AI Agent Is Given to Read Before It Acts
labs.summary: Treats the text handed to an AI agent as security-relevant input: checks where each piece came from and that the total stays within set limits.

labs.title: Investigating a False-Positive Alert in a Verification Script
labs.summary: Handling a noisy alert from my own tooling: reproduce it, find why it fires, narrow it, and keep a test so real problems are still caught.

labs.title: Linux User and Group Management for Access Control
labs.summary: Creating and removing Linux users and groups and assigning ownership, from a security analyst's point of view.

labs.title: SSH Brute-Force Investigation and Automated Defense
labs.summary: A full SSH brute-force exercise on a lab VM: run the attack, pull the evidence from the logs with shell tools, then watch Fail2ban detect and block it.

labs.title: Endpoint Process Chain Triage with Pipe-Delimited Logs and awk
labs.summary: SOC-style triage of a synthetic process-creation log, using Linux pipelines and awk to trace which process started which.

labs.title: HTTP in Practice (Pentester POV)
labs.summary: How a browser proves who it is and what the server trusts: sessions, cookies and headers, studied on real requests rather than exploited.

labs.title: Real SUID Behavior: Scripts vs Binaries
labs.summary: Tests how the SUID bit really behaves on a modern Linux system, and why it works on binaries but not on scripts.

labs.title: Linux Permissions & Ownership Hands-On Practice
labs.summary: Hands-on practice changing file permissions and ownership on Linux, and reading who can access what.

portfolio.title: Vulnerability Assessment of an Internet-Exposed Database (Training Scenario, NIST SP 800-30)
portfolio.summary: A scenario-based assessment of a business-critical MySQL database reachable from the internet: risks identified and prioritised with NIST SP 800-30, plus remediation and validation steps. No live system was touched.

portfolio.title: Letting Home Assistant Wake and Sleep a Mac Without Handing It Broad Access
portfolio.summary: Wake and sleep treated as two separate trust decisions: wake adds no new authority, and sleep goes through a local-only bridge that can run one fixed command.

portfolio.title: Proving a Backup Restores: Encrypted Off-Host Backup of an Agent's State
portfolio.summary: An encrypted off-machine backup of my agent's database, verified by restoring it on a second machine and checking structure, contents and integrity.

portfolio.title: Investigating an Unexplained Remote Shutdown and Locking Down the Power-Off Path
portfolio.summary: A Mac in my setup was powered off by a chat message with no clear cause. I traced the path that allowed it, closed it, and made shutdown default-deny with a record of every caller.

portfolio.title: Building an SSRF Guard for an Agent's Web Fetches, Then Finding Two Bypasses in It
portfolio.summary: I built the guard that stops an agent tool fetching internal addresses, ran an independent review of my own fix, and found two live bypasses before either was patched.

portfolio.title: Vetting Third-Party Tools Before Installing Them: Source, Permissions, Removal
portfolio.summary: How I evaluated candidate tools: pinned source revisions, comparison with a manual baseline, bounded trials, and clean removal for the ones that did not earn their place.

portfolio.title: Stopping an AI Agent from Claiming Success It Cannot Prove
portfolio.summary: The verification layer around my agent supervisor: success needs evidence, checks fail closed, decision changes are shadow-tested, and recovery is rehearsed.

portfolio.title: Sharing an Agent's Output Files Safely: Expiring Links and Hash Checks
portfolio.summary: A way to hand one task's report to one recipient without giving storage access: single-purpose expiring links, integrity checks before delivery, and durable delivery state.

portfolio.title: Supervising an AI Agent: Approvals, Audit Logs and Recovery Before It Acts
portfolio.summary: I designed and tested a supervision layer for a local AI agent: task-scoped permissions, approvals, audit records and restart-safe controls. Feature-flagged and fixture-tested, not live.

reports.title: WebCheckup Report: External Check-Up of juribuora.com, With Fixes and a Re-Test
reports.summary: I ran my own website check-up service against my own site. It found nine things. Four were fixed and one partly fixed, all re-measured the same day. Four are still open, and the tool got two things wrong.
